must_fire.case: that same record with one hex digit of its recorded sha256 changed
must_fire.chosen_by: derived from the silent case, so the two differ by one hex digit and by nothing else
must_fire.why: the recorded hash no longer equals the file on disk, which is the whole of what this gate judges. It reads diverged_body_unknown rather than diverged since 2026-08-11, and that is the point of it now: a byte-state nobody can produce is counted as debt and never as a pass, which is the live case for the rule that a repair may not turn an unanswerable question green

must_stay_silent.why: the file the artifact recorded reading is the file that is there now, so there is nothing for this gate to report

second_sign_must_fire.why: the numbers moved, which is the finding this gate exists for. calibration.why_the_debt_pair_is_anchored_on_the_pop: the declared list is the one thing in this file meant to be shortened until it is empty, so a case standing on it goes vacuous the day the last debt is repaid -- which is exactly how the pair written here on 2026-08-03 erased itself. retired.why: both cases named a live artifact, and the firing one went vacuous when the divergence it stood on was repaired: 0 diverged of 9 where 1 was expected. A calibration case anchored on a live defect erases itself the day somebody fixes the defect

calibration.why_it_cannot_go_vacuous: neither case names an artifact of the tree. The silent half is drawn from this run's own sweep by rule and the firing half is that same record with one hex digit changed, so a repair anywhere in the tree moves which record is used and never whether there is one. The single condition that would stop the pair running -- no matched input record in the whole tree -- is asserted as a failure rather than reported as a silence
